subject: Preflight: fleet-topology & traffic-cadence for Hyperlane pilot
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Marin <elena@hyperlane.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Preflight: fleet-topology & traffic-cadence for Hyperlane pilot

Hi Elena — great to speak yesterday. As we scope the Dedicated pilot for Hyperlane (HL-3492) we want to capture a compact traffic cartography so our GPU mix and tiling recommendations align with your burst windows and SLA targets. Quick asks we can start with: 

- Attach a 7-day sample of production traffic (UTC timestamps preferred). CSV with columns: timestamp, route, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, p90_latency_ms, user_id is ideal.
- Typical concurrency distribution (sessions per minute) and known peak days/timezones.
- Prompt/response length examples for the top 5 routes + expected change over 12 months.
- Any strict P99 latency SLA or cost constraints to weigh tradeoffs.

If you can drop the sample (token_hist + usage snapshot) we’ll run a quick tilt analysis and follow up with a recommended fleet topology and a short mutual action plan (timeline, pilot capacity, canary sizing). Camila, looping you for workload questions; Marissa I’ll need a pricing anchor after we size.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Marin <elena@hyperlane.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Gutierrez <carlos.g@hyperlane.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: fleet-topology & traffic-cadence for Hyperlane pilot

Jonas — thanks, attaching the 7-day extracts as requested. A few notes up front: 

- We have strong dayparting: primary peaks Monday morning (08:00-11:00 PT) and Thursday evening (18:00-20:00 PT). Peak day concurrency ~ 3.8k sessions/min across all routes.
- Top routes by volume: invoice-summarize, chat-assist, search-embed, doc-extract, rerank. Prompt tokens typically 12–60; response tokens 30–450 depending on summarization depth.
- P90 latency target for pilot: < 350ms for chat-assist; P99 can be relaxed to 1.2s for non-critical routes.
- Attached: hyperlane_token_hist_sample.csv (trimmed), hyperlane_usage_snapshot_202705.csv. The logs redacted user ids.

Let us know if you need raw KV cache traces or any extra fields. We’re aiming for a two-week pilot start window.

—Elena
Elena Marin
Head of Platform, Hyperlane

Attachments: hyperlane_token_hist_sample.csv (csv, 1.2MB), hyperlane_usage_snapshot_202705.csv (csv, 900KB)
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Marin <elena@hyperlane.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: fleet-topology & traffic-cadence for Hyperlane pilot

Thanks for the data, Elena — this is exactly what we need. Quick clarifying follow-ups so the topology recommendation is tight: 

1) Session shape: when you say 3.8k sessions/min peak, is that sustained for >30 minutes or microbursts of ~5–10 minutes inside the window? We size differently for sustained vs. spiky.
2) Abort/early-stop rate: do users commonly cut responses early (we see this as partial KV cache reuse opportunities)? If you have % of sessions that end before 60% of expected response tokens, send a rough figure.
3) Route SLOs: you listed a P90 and P99 targets — can you confirm whether chat-assist has priority routing (must-hit 350ms during pilot) or if it’s a guideline? This affects pinning to lower-latency nodes vs. cost-optimized pooled nodes.
4) Model variants: are you planning to use a single model family across routes or mix (e.g., 2x Llama2-13B for chat + 1x smaller quantized embedding model)? If mixed, sample mapping helps (route->model).

Proposal for next step (mutual action plan):
- We’ll run a quick occupancy and burst-slab simulation within 48 hours and return a 1-page fleet topology (GPU types + recommended oversubscription) + cost delta table.
- You review and optionally provide KV cache traces (if available) for a deeper caching analysis.
- Pilot kickoff: provision N days of reserved capacity, do smoke tests with your dev traffic, then open canary to 2% of production.

I’ll run the simulation and attach a draft SLA for review (redwood_sla-draft-v1.pdf). If you confirm the sustained vs burst shape we’ll lock the pilot capacity recommendation.

Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_sla-draft-v1.pdf (pdf, 250KB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Marin <elena@hyperlane.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: fleet-topology & traffic-cadence for Hyperlane pilot

Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround and the sample attachments. Summary & next steps: 

- Action: Camila will deliver the occupancy/burst simulation and two fleet options (low-latency pinned profile and cost-optimized pooled profile) by Mon EOD (48h).
- Action: Hyperlane to confirm sustained vs microburst characterization and share any available early-stop metrics by EOD Mon.
- Pricing: Marissa will prepare a draft reserved-capacity anchor after Camila posts the topology; expect that in 2 business days.
- Pilot timeline: target start week of Jun 21, smoke tests on reserved nodes before canary.

I’ll also add the HubSpot deal (HL-3492) notes and link to the SLA draft. If the data shows heavy short-lived microbursts we’ll recommend a modest overprovision + burst pool to reduce p99 tail risk. Otherwise we may recommend a weight of quantized embedding servers + 1.5x baseline GPU commitment for peak.

Thanks — Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
